name: The Slammer

tenures.source: CyberSlam's own Newbies page stages his arrival - "like a gift from God, The Slammer walked through the stadium doors and became President" - and credits him with naming Slammers, naming Slammin, and creating the monthly CSlam event (/promotions/cyberslam/archive/newbies-the-story-of-cyberslam-1998.html). The staff panel on the hub's own Mail Box page heads its list "Slammer (President)" (/promotions/cyberslam/archive/mail-box-and-staff-panel-1998.html), and his signature closes the Join, Transfer, Slammers, Create-a-Slammer, news-board entrance and CWO entrance pages. By the front-page staff panel of September 1999 the office reads "President: Funky Nassau" instead.
tenures.note: An office, held in the hub's own fiction: he bans a wrestler, sanctions another, sets the purse and signs the paperwork. The record does not say how the office changed hands.

caption: CyberSlam's own President from its first year: the figure its origin story has walking through the stadium doors to take charge, who named the players Slammers, named the game Slammin, and put a monthly title at the end of it.

name: Funky Nassau

tenures.role: CWF Commissioner, CWF league President, later President of CyberSlam
tenures.source: The 1998 rulebook names him twice - "CWF (Funky Nassau)" in its commissioner block, and in full in its own section on the indy feds: "Currently Nassau is the commissioner of the CWF fed and the president of the CWF league" (/promotions/cyberslam/archive/guidelines-and-faqs-1998.html). The staff panel on the Mail Box page lists "Nassau (CWF Commissioner)" (/promotions/cyberslam/archive/mail-box-and-staff-panel-1998.html). The front page of September 1999 reads "President: Funky Nassau" (/promotions/cyberslam/archive/fed-directory-the-universe-of-feds-2000.html). He is still deciding the game's business in January 2001, a news post recording "an agreement with Funky Nassau" to fire an absent commissioner (/promotions/cyberslam/archive/news-2036-imwa-commish-skull-gone.html).
tenures.note: The one office-holder the record follows across the whole run, from a single fed's commissioner to the President of the game.

caption: Commissioner of the CWF and president of its league in CyberSlam's first rulebook, President of the whole game by 1999, and still the authority a member fed's commissioner had to answer to three weeks before the hub closed.
